issues.description: Field 'numberOfTutors' has conflicting types: the exercise UML in problem_statement.md declares numberOfTutors as type int (Lecture class attribute), but the solution implementation declares the field as 'private short numberOfTutors;'. This difference changes the expected attribute type and propagates to API signatures students must implement, causing confusion when following the UML/API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute type consistent. Preferred fix: change the solution field to 'private int numberOfTutors;' so it matches the UML and the rest of the documented API. Alternatively, if 'short' is intentional, update the problem statement/UML and all documentation/tests to declare numberOfTutors as short.

issues.description: Constructor parameter type for the 'numberOfTutors' argument differs: the problem statement/UML implies an int attribute (so the constructor parameter should be int), but the solution constructor declares the parameter as 'short numberOfTutors' in its signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter with the UML attribute type. Change the solution constructor signature to use an int parameter for numberOfTutors (e.g., '... int numberOfTutors') and assign it to an int field. If short is required, update the UML and problem text accordingly.

issues.description: Setter parameter type for setNumberOfTutors differs from the UML-implied type: the solution declares 'public void setNumberOfTutors(short numberOfTutors)', while the UML and problem description indicate numberOfTutors should be an int, so callers and students will expect a setter that accepts an int.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the solution setter to accept int (public void setNumberOfTutors(int numberOfTutors)) and store it in an int field so signatures match the UML and avoid mismatches between expected API and implementation. Alternatively, document and update the UML to use short consistently.
